title: Local adjustments
description: Touch up just one part of the photo. Choose where to act (the mask) and what to change: for example, brighten the faint areas of a nebula without blowing out the core, or bring out the red of hydrogen while leaving the stars alone. Local adjustments are applied after all the other corrections and also end up in the exported image.
noObject: No recognized object has a position in the image: use “Plate solve” in the Objects step, or choose “Circle” and place it by hand.

add.label: + Add
add.hint: Adds a local adjustment, with a mask on the faint areas

empty: No local adjustments. Press “Add” to create one: you can have up to {max}.
noImage: Open an image to use local adjustments.

layer.select: Select this adjustment to edit it
layer.disable: Turn off this adjustment without removing it, to compare

showMask.label: Show the mask in red
showMask.hint: Colors red the area where the adjustment acts: the redder, the stronger. Useful while you choose and tune the mask.

brightness.label: Light
brightness.hint: Acts only on parts within a certain brightness, for example to brighten faint areas without touching an already bright core.

color.label: Color
color.hint: Acts only on parts of a certain color: for example the red of hydrogen or the cyan of oxygen.

stars.label: Stars
stars.hint: Acts on the stars found in the image, with a circle that grows with their brightness. With “Invert the mask” it acts on everything except the stars.

object.label: Object
object.hint: Acts within a feathered ellipse around the main object recognized in the field.

linear.label: Gradient
linear.hint: Full effect on one side, fading out completely. Useful when the sky is brighter on one side.

radial.label: Circle
radial.hint: Full effect at the center of an ellipse, fading toward the edge.

whole.label: By hand
whole.hint: No automatic mask: you paint the area with the brush.

red.name: Red
red.hint: The red of hydrogen (H-alpha), the most common color in emission nebulae

cyan.name: Cyan
cyan.hint: The blue-green of oxygen (OIII), for example in planetary nebulae

blue.name: Blue
blue.hint: The blue of reflection nebulae and galaxy arms

yellow.name: Yellow
yellow.hint: The yellow-orange of cool stars and galaxy cores

magenta.name: Magenta
magenta.hint: The pink-magenta where hydrogen and oxygen overlap

green.name: Green
green.hint: Green, which in astrophotos is almost always a cast to remove

faint.name: Faint parts
faint.hint: Background and faint areas, to bring them out without touching the rest

midtones.name: Midtones
midtones.hint: The intermediate tones, where the structure of nebulae lies

bright.name: Bright parts
bright.hint: Cores and stars, to darken them and recover their detail

none.label: Pan
none.hint: The mouse pans and zooms the image, as usual

brush.label: Brush
brush.hint: Paint on the photo the area where the adjustment should act

light.fromHint: Below this brightness the adjustment does not act. At 0% it includes black too.
light.toHint: Above this brightness the adjustment does not act. At 100% it includes white too.

hue.label: Hue
hue.hint: The color to act on, around the color wheel: 0° red, 60° yellow, 120° green, 180° cyan, 240° blue, 300° magenta.
hue.eyedropperHint: Click a point on the photo and its hue becomes the mask’s hue
hue.eyedropper: Pick the color from the photo
hue.widthHint: How far the selection extends around the hue. Narrow for a precise color, wide for the whole family of nearby colors.
hue.note: Grays and the dark background are always left out, because there the color is just noise.

stars.sizeHint: Widens or narrows the circle around each star. The circle is already larger for brighter stars, which have a wider halo.
stars.found: {count} stars found. With “Invert the mask” the adjustment acts on everything except the stars.
stars.pending: The star search starts as soon as the adjustment changes something or the mask is shown.

geometry.recenterHint: Puts the ellipse back on the main object recognized in the field
geometry.drawLinearHint: Drag on the photo: where you press the effect is full, where you release it ends
geometry.drawRadialHint: Drag on the photo: where you press is the center, the distance at which you release is the radius
geometry.radiusHint: The radius of the ellipse, along the major axis.
geometry.elongationHint: 1 is a circle; lower values flatten the ellipse, to follow an edge-on galaxy.
geometry.linearNote: The solid line shows where the effect is full, the dashed line where it ends.

feather.label: Edge feathering
feather.hint: How soft the transition is between where the adjustment acts and where it does not. Soft edges give touch-ups that go unnoticed.

intensity.label: Intensity
intensity.hint: How strongly the adjustment acts inside the mask. At 50% it has half the effect.

invert.label: Invert the mask
invert.hint: Swaps inside and outside, so the adjustment acts where it did not before. For example, an inverted “Stars” mask acts on everything except the stars.

paint.title: Paint by hand
paint.wholeNote: Paint on the photo the area to act on. The mouse wheel and right button still zoom and pan.
paint.optionalNote: Optional. Paint to restrict the mask chosen above to an area; the adjustment acts only where both apply.
paint.sizeHint: The brush diameter on screen. If you zoom into the photo, you paint more finely.
paint.hardnessHint: Low for a soft, fading edge, high for a sharp edge.
paint.opacityHint: How much each stroke covers. With low values you build up the mask little by little, one stroke over another.
paint.fillHint: Fills the whole painted area. Then use the eraser to remove the parts to exclude
paint.removeHint: Removes the hand painting and keeps only the mask chosen above

adjust.brightnessHint: Brightens or darkens the area. When brightening, tones approach white without clipping it; when darkening, blacks stay black.
adjust.contrastHint: More contrast separates the tones of the area better; less contrast softens it.
adjust.saturationHint: Makes the colors of the area more intense or more muted; at -1 the area turns gray.
adjust.vibranceHint: Mainly boosts the muted colors of the area and leaves already vivid ones almost untouched.
adjust.temperatureHint: Shifts the color of the area toward warm (yellow-orange) or cool (blue).
adjust.tintHint: Shifts the color of the area toward magenta (positive values) or green (negative). Useful against a local green cast.
adjust.sharpnessHint: Enhances fine details only in the area, for example the structure of a nebula, and keeps the background smooth.
adjust.noiseReductionHint: Smooths the grain only in the area, for example the sky background, and keeps the object sharp.
adjust.resetHint: Resets the “What changes” sliders to zero and leaves the mask as it is
